chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next year, except if he attends 'Arafat."

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat (the site of the standing during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of forgiveness in Ramadan and the exception of 'Arafat?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique spiritual efficacy of Ramadan as a decisive window for divine pardon, where missed opportunities are not easily repeated. The exception of standing at 'Arafat (*wuquf*) serves as a profound theological link, suggesting that the sincere devotion of Hajj can compensate for or extend the mercy missed during the fasting month, reinforcing the interconnectedness of Ramadan and Hajj in achieving salvation.
